subject.title: security fix(gateway): defend pre-auth device-signature verify against CPU DoS

question: Should OpenClaw accept this layered pre-auth device-signature hardening as the canonical fix for the linked gateway CPU-DoS issue?
rationale: The code appears technically sound, but it changes unauthenticated auth validation, lockout behavior, and protocol rejection semantics, which requires gateway/security owner intent before merge.

options.title: Accept After Proof
options.body: Ask for current-head real behavior proof and green exact-head checks, then merge if the gateway/security owner accepts the stricter boundary.

options.title: Narrow The Mitigation
options.body: Keep the schema/helper hardening but ask the author to adjust limiter semantics if maintainers are worried about lockout behavior for legitimate bursts.

options.title: Replace With Owner Patch
options.body: Pause this contributor branch and land an owner-authored variant if security disclosure or release timing needs a different path.

recommendation.title: Accept After Proof
recommendation.body: Ask for current-head real behavior proof and green exact-head checks, then merge if the gateway/security owner accepts the stricter boundary.
